title:
Step 4 of 10:
The *refuse* list.
sub: The short set of uses where no amount of control makes it acceptable. Agree them once, in advance.

title:
Decide these before
someone asks.
text:
Without a list, every request becomes a negotiation, and the answer quietly depends on who is asking and how senior they are.

With a list, the answer is the same on a Friday afternoon as it is in a steering meeting.

title:
Five that belong on
almost every list:
items: AI *signing* a record or applying an electronic signature
AI *releasing* a batch, a lot or a product
AI *closing* a deviation or CAPA on its own
AI making a *clinical decision* that affects a patient
AI *writing to a validated record* with no human signature gate

title:
What makes it a refusal
rather than a high tier?
text:
A high tier means more control makes it acceptable.

A refusal is where the thing being removed *is* the control. The human judgement was the safeguard, and automating it does not leave a smaller safeguard behind. It leaves none.
tag: Not a risk level. A different question

title:
Never "policy
says no."
text:
Say what would have to be true instead, and offer the shape next door.

*"The model cannot approve the deviation. It can draft the assessment, show the matching procedure text, and prepare it for your signature. Same time saved, and the accountability stays where it has to."*
tag: Almost every refusal has a permitted version

title:
Then put the list in
the procedure.
text:
A refuse list that lives in one person's head is an opinion, and it gets overruled.

In an SOP it stops being personal. It protects the person who has to say no, and it answers the question before it is asked.

title: Keep it short.
text:
A refuse list of twenty items is a ban with extra steps, and teams will route around it.

Five items, firmly held, buys credibility for every yes you give. That is the trade: be absolute about very little, so you can be flexible about the rest.

title:
Step 5 next week:
requirements that can fail.
text:
An AI requirement that cannot fail cannot be validated. Next step is writing ones that can.

Forward this to whoever is being asked these questions today.
